derivation_notes: The parent assumption that colonization efficiency is independent of current extinction susceptibility is relaxed by letting stress reduce propagule production or establishment through a bounded nonlinear penalty. The exponential factor keeps colonization positive while creating a genuine p-by-extinction_rate interaction in the scored dp_dt mapping.
change_summary: Colonization is now directly suppressed by the current extinction susceptibility state, not just opposed by the separate extinction loss term. This adds stress-dependent interaction and curvature to the occupancy-growth law while recovering the parent when stress sensitivity is zero.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Colonization efficiency is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Landscape-wide stressors that elevate local extinction risk often simultaneously reduce fecundity, disperser availability, or establishment success, coupling extinction susceptibility to colonization effectiveness.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set colonization_stress_sensitivity = 0 to recover the parent colonization law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The colonization contribution to dp_dt is a product of p(1-p) and a facilitation/interference factor that depends only on p, so the effect of occupancy on target growth is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state except for the separate linear subtraction -extinction_rate*p.
response_change.child_relation: Let colonization efficiency itself be modulated by the current extinction susceptibility state, so the occupancy effect on dp_dt changes with both p and extinction_rate. This creates a state-dependent interaction in which the same occupancy can yield different colonization gains under different ecological stress histories.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed p in the intermediate occupancy range, trajectories with elevated extinction_rate show reduced net growth not only through larger losses but also through weaker colonization recovery, producing slower rebound and stronger asymmetry between expansion and decline phases.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Most visible when 0<p<1, especially at intermediate occupancy where colonization is active, and when extinction_rate varies appreciably along the observed trajectory because the existing relaxation dynamics have been displaced from low-stress equilibrium.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as altered rebound slope after episodes that raise extinction_rate; in holdout, the same interaction extends to stronger history dependence where equal p values have different dp_dt because extinction_rate differs.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the stress effect on colonization is set to zero, so colonization depends only on p and extinction acts only through the existing subtraction term.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Landscape-wide stressors that elevate local extinction risk often simultaneously reduce fecundity, disperser availability, or establishment success, coupling extinction susceptibility to colonization effectiveness.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because extinction_rate first enters a saturating stress load and then passes through a nonlinear exponential attenuation that multiplies the existing p-dependent colonization branch, so the colonization curve itself shifts with stress rather than merely being uniformly rescaled once for all conditions.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Colonization efficiency is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Current extinction susceptibility nonlinearly suppresses colonization efficiency through a bounded stress-response factor.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set colonization_stress_sensitivity = 0 to recover the parent exactly because exp(0) = 1.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare times along one trajectory where p is similar and intermediate but extinction_rate differs due to its lagged dynamics. The parent predicts the same colonization contribution at those matched p values, with only the additive loss term changing; the child predicts an extra depression of the colonization branch at higher extinction_rate, yielding slower rebound and lower dp_dt than additive loss alone.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this matched-p contrast because its colonization term is strictly a function of p and fixed parameters. Refitting colonization_rate, colonization_density_dependence, or colonization_saturation_scale only changes one shared p-only curve, so it cannot make colonization at the same p differ across conditions with different extinction_rate.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Most visible when 0<p<1, especially at intermediate occupancy where colonization is active, and when extinction_rate varies appreciably along the observed trajectory because the existing relaxation dynamics have been displaced from low-stress equilibrium.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as altered rebound slope after episodes that raise extinction_rate; in holdout, the same interaction extends to stronger history dependence where equal p values have different dp_dt because extinction_rate differs.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the stress effect on colonization is set to zero, so colonization depends only on p and extinction acts only through the existing subtraction term.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that extinction susceptibility affects occupancy change only by removing occupied patches and does not also impair propagule production or establishment from surviving occupied patches.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Colonization efficiency is independent of the current extinction susceptibility state.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Landscape-wide stressors that elevate local extinction risk often simultaneously reduce fecundity, disperser availability, or establishment success, coupling extinction susceptibility to colonization effectiveness.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the assumption that stressed metapopulations lose patches faster but colonize just as effectively. In the parent, if p is held fixed, changing extinction_rate changes dp_dt only through the linear loss term -extinction_rate*p; the colonization branch has the same slope and curvature regardless of stress history. In the child, extinction_rate would also modulate colonization, so the mapping from observed states to dp_dt acquires a genuine p-by-extinction_rate interaction. Observable condition: compare times along one trajectory where p is similar but extinction_rate differs because of the existing lagged extinction dynamics; hold colonization parameters fixed. Parent prediction: the colonization contribution is identical at those matched p values. Child prediction: higher extinction_rate depresses colonization gain, so net growth is lower than a pure additive loss change would imply, especially during recovery from high-stress periods. This is admissible without new states because extinction_rate already exists and varies dynamically. The contrast targets the scored mapping directly, not only the auxiliary extinction_rate trajectory. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this across such matched-p but differing-extinction_rate conditions, because its colonization term has no dependence on extinction_rate at all; refitting can only change the common p-only curve, not make it shift with stress.

scenario_text: Track the fraction of habitat patches occupied by a focal population across a landscape of otherwise equivalent patches. Occupied patches seed colonization of empty patches, while local population loss turns occupied patches into empty ones. The target is the instantaneous change in regional occupancy along one trajectory.
